extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on preparing, submitting, and examining affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 (and interplay with 1.132) to antedate references and overcome rejections in U.S. patent prosecution. Covers who may make affidavits, formal requirements, evidence and exhibits, genus/species rules, and limits (e.g., when affidavits are ineffective).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper rule for affidavits/declarations (1.131 vs 1.132)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 may be used to establish that the subject matter relied on in the reference was the invention of the applicant; affidavits/declarations submitted for that purpose are properly filed under 37 CFR 1.132 rather than 1.131, although those submitted improperly under 1.131 will be considered as though filed under 1.132 to traverse a ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re DeBaun and MPEP § 716.10 for discussion. A 1.132 showing is used to show the reference is a publication of applicant's own invention; a misfiled 1.131 will be treated as a 1.132 when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common assignee does not by itself antedate reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere fact that the reference patent or application publication and the application are owned by the same assignee does not avoid the necessity of filing an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 in the absence of a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that the patentee derived the subject matter from the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common ownership does not give rights that would not exist absent common ownership. However, a showing that the inventions were commonly owned or subject to an obligation of assignment at the time the later invention was made may preclude rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102(f)/103 or 102(g)/103 (see MPEP §§ 706.02(l), 706.02(l)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference is publication of applicant's own invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on a publication may be overcome by a showing that it was published either by applicant himself/herself or on his/her behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because this showing is not to establish a date of invention under 37 CFR 1.131, limitations in 35 U.S.C. 104 and 37 CFR 1.131(a)(1) regarding country of acts (NAFTA/WTO) are not applicable. See Ex parte Lemieux and MPEP § 716.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-authorship: applicant as author or sole inventor on publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant is one of the co-authors of a publication cited against the application, the applicant may overcome the rejection by filing an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 or a specific affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 establishing that the article describes applicant's own work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An affidavit by applicant alone indicating applicant is the sole inventor and others were merely working under his/her direction is sufficient to remove the publication as a reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(a). See In re Katz.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation: show patentee derived disclosure from applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: When unclaimed subject matter of a patent, application publication, or other publication is applicant's own invention, the rejection may be removed by evidence establishing that the patentee/applicant/author derived the relevant subject matter from applicant and that applicant made the invention on which the disclosure is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases: In re Mathews; In re Facius. Evidence must establish both derivation and that applicant made the invention underlying the disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities applied against claims: antedating uses/knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on an activity showing that the claimed invention was used or known prior to the filing date may be overcome by an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 establishing a date of invention prior to the date of the activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, applicant(s) may file a specific affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 showing that the activity was performed by the applicant(s). Statutory bars are exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: How much of the claimed invention must be shown
rubrics_metrics.description: The 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit or declaration must establish possession of either the whole invention claimed or something falling within the claim (such as a species of a claimed genus), in the sense that the claim as a whole reads on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If differences between the claimed invention and the reference are so small as to render the claims obvious, an affidavit under 1.131 need only show no more than the reference shows. Examples: In re Tanczyn, In re Stryker, In re Wakefield. Affidavit need not show identical disclosure but must show completion commensurate with the extent of the invention as claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Swearing behind one of a plurality of combined references
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may overcome a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection based on a combination of references by showing completion of the invention prior to the effective date of any of the references; the affidavit must show possession of the whole invention or something within the claim prior to the effective date of the reference being antedated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant need not antedate with the earliest filing date among combined references. The affidavit must not merely show what one reference happens to show if that reference does not teach the basic inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of earlier secondary reference teachings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 based on Reference A in view of Reference B, with B earlier than A, the applicant can rely on teachings of Reference B to show that differences between applicant's 1.131 evidence and the claimed invention would have been obvious prior to the date of Reference A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nevertheless, the 1.131 affidavit/declaration must still establish possession of the claimed invention, not just what Reference A shows, if Reference A does not teach the basic inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule as to generic claims (species antedates genus)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference or activity applied against generic claims may (in most cases) be antedated as to such claims by an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 showing completion of the invention of only a single species, within the genus, prior to the effective date of the reference or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Ex parte Biesecker and cases. Distinguish unpredictable arts (see MPEP § 715.03) where species may not support genus antedating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus-species and predictability considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: When generic claims are rejected on a reference disclosing a species not antedated by the affidavit, the affidavit will not ordinarily be withdrawn unless applicant establishes possession of the generic invention prior to the effective date; the affidavit must show as much as the minimum disclosure required by a patent specification to support a generic claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reference discloses several species of a claimed genus, applicant must show prior completion of all species shown in the reference to overcome directly under 1.131. Indirect antedating possible by showing other species made that make the reference species obvious. Tests consider predictability and size of genus (e.g., halogens example). Cases: In re Plumb, In re Schaub, In re Shokal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species versus embodiments distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: References or activities that disclose one or more embodiments of a single claimed invention (as opposed to species of a claimed genus) can be overcome by a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit showing prior completion of a single embodiment of the invention, whether same or different from that disclosed in the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Fong and In re Defano. The inquiry distinguishes whether the reference discloses separate species of a genus or merely different embodiments of the same invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may make affidavit or declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties who may make an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 include: (A) all the inventors of the subject matter claimed; (B) less than all named inventors where shown they invented the subject matter under rejection; (C) a party qualified under 37 CFR 1.42, 1.43, or 1.47 when some inventors unavailable or incapable; (D) the assignee or other party in interest when it is not possible to produce the affidavit/declaration of the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where fewer than all inventors sign, the affidavit must show completion of the invention by all joint inventors of the subject matter of the rejected claims. Signatures of remaining joint inventors are sufficient if a joint inventor is deceased, refuses to sign, or is otherwise unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements of affidavits and declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit is a statement in writing made under oath before an authorized officer; 37 CFR 1.68 permits a declaration in lieu of an affidavit which must include acknowledgment that willful false statements are punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001 and may jeopardize the application/patent; the declarant must state that all statements of his/her own knowledge are true and statements made on information and belief are believed to be true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 604-604.06 for additional formal requirements of affidavits.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. patent or application publication claiming same invention — remedy and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When the reference is a noncommonly owned U.S. patent or patent application publication claiming the same invention as applicant and its publication date is less than 1 year prior to the presentation of claims to that invention in the application being examined, applicant's remedy, if any, must be by way of 37 CFR 1.608 (interference) instead of 37 CFR 1.131.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If publication date is 1 year or more prior to presentation of claims, a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 135(b) should be made. Form paragraphs 23.14 and 23.14.01 may be used. Note the conditions for use in Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.131 ineffective where reference claims same patentable invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit is ineffective to overcome a U.S. patent or patent application publication not only where there is a verbatim correspondence between claims, but also where there is no patentable distinction between the respective claims; an applicant claiming an invention identical to or obvious in view of the invention claimed in a domestic patent/publication cannot employ an affidavit under 1.131 to avoid an interference with the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The concept of 'same patentable invention' follows 37 CFR 1.601(n). Ex parte Eickmeyer and related case law explain that an affidavit cannot be used to avoid declaring an interference; applicant may instead pursue interference remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential requirement: show facts (not conclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The essential thing to be shown under 37 CFR 1.131 is priority of invention and this may be done by any satisfactory evidence of the fact. FACTS, not conclusions, must be alleged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A general allegation of prior completion, or a declaration asserting only that facts exist without detailing them, is insufficient. See Ex parte Saunders and In re Harry. The affidavit must set out the factual basis for claims of conception/reduction and dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible exhibits and how to support affidavit
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits that may accompany an affidavit include sketches, blueprints, photographs, reproductions of notebook entries, models, supporting statements by witnesses, testimony in an interference, and disclosure documents; each exhibit relied upon should be specifically referred to in the affidavit or declaration in terms of what it is relied upon to show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibits and models must comply with 37 CFR 1.91 to be entered into an application file. An accompanying exhibit need not support all claimed limitations provided missing limitations are supported by the declaration itself. See Ex parte Ovshinsky.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original exhibits and explanation if absent
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.131(b) requires that original exhibits of drawings or records, or photocopies thereof, accompany and form part of the affidavit or declaration or their absence satisfactorily explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If originals were made and lost, reproduce and furnish them; if relying on verbal disclosures, state as nearly as possible the language used. See Ex parte Donovan. Dates removed from exhibits can be addressed in the oath/declaration body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of dates and diligence requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When alleging conception or reduction to practice prior to the effective date of the reference, the affidavit may state actual dates or allege that the acts occurred prior to a specified date; however, actual dates of acts relied on to establish diligence must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there has not been reduction to practice prior to the date of the reference, applicant must show diligence in completion from a time just prior to the reference date continuously up to the date of reduction to practice or up to filing (constructive reduction). See MPEP § 715.07(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three ways to show prior invention under 37 CFR 1.131(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The showing must be sufficient to show: (A) reduction to practice prior to the effective date of the reference; or (B) conception prior to the effective date coupled with due diligence from prior to the reference date to a subsequent actual reduction to practice; or (C) conception prior to the effective date coupled with due diligence from prior to the reference date to the filing date of the application (constructive reduction to practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conception is the mental part of the inventive act but must be definite and capable of proof. Conception alone confers no rights unless followed by reasonable diligence to an act such as reduction to practice or filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to practice and utility proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof of actual reduction to practice generally requires showing the apparatus actually existed and worked for its intended purpose, though some devices are simple enough that mere construction suffices; proof of utility must be shown under 1.131 only if the reference discloses a utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether test results are required depends on facts of each case; ultimate issue is whether one of ordinary skill would be satisfied to a reasonable certainty of the alleged utility. Cases: In re Asahi/America; In re Wilkinson; In re Blake.

rubrics_metrics.name: 131 practice parallels but is not controlled by interference law
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the tests for sufficiency of an affidavit under Rule 131(b) parallels interference practice concepts (conception, diligence, reduction to practice), 131 practice is not necessarily controlled by interference law and the requirements may differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In re Eickmeyer:  purpose of 131 affidavit is to antedate the effective date of a reference; the 'conception' and 'reduction to practice' required under the rule need not be identical to interference standards. See In re Borkowski for further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit/exhibit specificity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit/declaration and exhibits must clearly explain which facts or data applicant is relying on to show completion prior to the particular date; vague and general statements about what exhibits describe accompanied by a general assertion of reduction to practice do not satisfy 37 CFR 1.131(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must give a clear explanation pointing out exactly what facts are established and relied upon. See In re Borkowski and related cases for insufficiency of vague allegations.
